This is the opening of Surah an-Najm (53), verse 1, from Sayyid Qutb's commentary Fi Zilal al-Quran.

In this passage we are on a lofty, luminous and fluttering horizon, where the heart of Muhammad (ﷺ) spent a few beautiful and radiant moments in the company of the Higher Realm. It is a melody made of very gentle, soft waves that come together in harmony. We hear the colours, the allusions and the signs of those enchanting moments. The words, their musicality and their atmosphere are all enchanting.

These are the experiences of the heart of Muhammad (ﷺ), moments in which all veils were removed from before his eyes, and he was receiving guidance and revelation from the Higher Realm, seeing and hearing. His heart was memorising. Only the polished heart of Muhammad (ﷺ) would truly feel what those moments were like, but by the grace of Allah He has expressed this experience in words for us, His servants: in a highly impactful manner, with a music that flows like water, in which the colours, allusions, atmosphere and signs have been conveyed to us. This was the journey of that polished heart, and it was within the vastness of the Higher Realm. Every single step is coming before our eyes as a picture: every scene, every step, in such a way that it is as though we are seeing it right now.

The passage begins with an oath.

﴿وَالنَّجْمِ إِذَا هَوَىٰ﴾ (53:1) "By the star when it sets."

The star sets, drawing near the earth, and an oath is sworn by it. What the oath is sworn upon is that Hazrat Jibra'il was thus:

﴿وَهُوَ بِالْأُفُقِ الْأَعْلَىٰ * ثُمَّ دَنَا فَتَدَلَّىٰ * فَكَانَ قَابَ قَوْسَيْنِ أَوْ أَدْنَىٰ * فَأَوْحَىٰ إِلَىٰ عَبْدِهِ مَا أَوْحَىٰ﴾ (53:7-10) "While he was on the highest horizon. Then he approached and descended, and was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer. And He revealed to His servant what He revealed."

Thus there is complete harmony and unity between the movement of the star and the movement of Hazrat Jibra'il. In this way, the atmosphere, movement and rhythm flow from the very beginning of the scene.

Regarding the verse ﴿وَالنَّجْمِ إِذَا هَوَىٰ﴾ (53:1), various interpretations have been related. The most apparent meaning is that it refers to the star Sirius (al-Shi'ra), since some Arabs worshipped it, and later mention of it occurs in this same surah:

﴿وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ رَبُّ الشِّعْرَىٰ﴾ (53:49) "And that He is the Lord of Sirius."

Ancient people gave great importance to the star Sirius. It is well known that the ancient Egyptians said that when Sirius crossed the highest heavens, a flood of water would come in the Nile. Therefore they kept watching Sirius and noting its movement. There are countless legends about it in the traditions of both the Persians and the Arabs. Hence the star here means this very Sirius, and there is also an intended correspondence between the oath and the thing sworn upon, which is evident in the setting of this star. Furthermore, the intention here is also to indicate that however great a star may be, it sets and disappears. Worship is due only to One who is not subject to decline and setting. This was the oath; now comes the matter upon which the oath is sworn.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 53, verses 2–4:

...﴿Your companion has neither strayed nor been misled. Nor does he speak from [his own] desire. It is nothing but a revelation that is revealed.﴾ (53:2–4)

Your companion is upon the right path; he has not gone astray. He is upon the straight way and is not walking any crooked path. He is sincere and is not self-seeking. He conveys the truth; he is neither a visionary deluded by illusions, nor a fabricator, nor an innovator, and in what he conveys to you, his own whims and desires have no part. He says only what is revealed, and he is truthful and trustworthy. Therefore he conveys the truth.

The bearers of this revelation are known, its method is fixed, and the one who brings it was seen by the Messenger (ﷺ) with his own eyes. This is not a vague matter, nor has he been deceived by some unseen power.

**Allamahu shadeedul-quwa ............ ma yaghsha (61) (35:4 to 61)**

"﴿He was taught by one mighty in power, endowed with wisdom. He appeared while he was on the highest horizon. Then he drew near and came down, until he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer. Then he revealed to His servant what he revealed. The heart did not lie about what it saw. Will you then dispute with him about what he sees?﴾"

Who are these "shadeed al-quwa" (the mighty in power) and "dhu mirrah" (possessor of strength)? They are Hadrat Jibreel (peace be upon him). He taught the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) the revelation (wahy, divine revelation) that he conveyed to him. This is the path and this is the journey, and all the stages and positions of this path are clear. On the high horizon he stood upright. The Prophet (ﷺ) saw him. This is the scene of the beginning of revelation, when the Prophet (ﷺ) saw Jibreel (peace be upon him) in the form in which Allah created him. He is of a very great created form. When he appeared to the Prophet, he filled the entire horizon. He gradually drew closer to the Prophet and came very near, within a distance of two bow-lengths or even less. In that close state, he conveyed to the Prophet's heart what he had to convey, and he delivered it. The phrase "what he had to reveal" is a general expression that points to the greatness of the revelation. That is, the manifestation of Jibreel (peace be upon him) occurred on the distant high horizon, but he delivered the revelation after coming extremely close. Therefore there is no doubt in its reception and acceptance.

Hadrat Muhammad (ﷺ) saw Hadrat Jibreel (peace be upon him) in a state that was a very certain state. In this seeing there was no ambiguity, no possibility of error, and no room for doubt or dispute.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 53, verses 11–15:

"The heart did not lie about what it saw" (11). "Will you then dispute with him about what he sees?" (53:12). The sight of the eye was not alone; the heart also saw. Deception of the sight is possible, but deception of the heart is not. He saw, and his heart was certain that this was an angel, the bearer of revelation, sent by Allah to convey revelation to him so that he might deliver it. This dispute is now ended, because his heart has accepted this reality, and he is the truthful and trustworthy one (al-Sadiq al-Amin).

Then Muhammad (ﷺ) saw this angel not only once. He saw him a second time as well.

"And indeed, he saw him another time, near the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha), near which is the Garden of Refuge (Jannat al-Ma'wa). When the Lote-tree was covered with that which covered it, his sight did not waver, nor did it transgress. Indeed he saw of the greatest signs of his Lord" (53:13–18). (Qur'anic quotations rendered in plain meaning.)

According to clear narrations, this event took place on the night of the Mi'raj (Ascension). Hadrat Jibril (علیہ السلام) (peace be upon him) came near to him, and he was in the form and shape in which Allah had created him. At that time he was near Sidrat al-Muntaha. Sidrah is a tree, the lote tree (Ber tree). Al-Muntaha means the place where a limit ends, and there is the Jannat al-Ma'wa. This is the place up to which the Prophet's mount went on the night of the Mi'raj, where the companionship of the Messenger (ﷺ) and Jibril (علیہ السلام) ended, where Jibril stopped, and where Hadrat Muhammad (ﷺ) went beyond it, to a point closer to the Throne of the Lord. In any case, all these matters belong to the realm of the higher world and the unseen. Their reality is known to Allah, or to His servant, al-Mustafa. We know only as much as the narrations tell us. If there were no narration, human intellects could not gallop their horses in this domain. A person can know on this subject only what he receives from Allah Ta'ala, who is the Creator of the angels and the Creator of man, and who knows well the characteristics of both.

However, here Allah Ta'ala has described some conditions of Sidrat al-Muntaha so that the matter becomes certain, and in order to make this journey definite and emphatic.

The passage begins: "When there covered the Lote-tree that which covered it" (53:16). The text is the Urdu rendering of Sayyid Qutb's commentary; the verse fragment quoted is the opening of verse 16.

Translation:

﴿When there covered the Lote-tree that which covered it﴾ (53:16). Details of what was covering it have not been given, nor has it been specified what it was that covered it. It was something so great and awe-inspiring that it is difficult to describe, and difficult to identify. In short, it was a great reality.

This also is a certain and established reality.

"The eye did not waver, nor did it transgress its limit" (53:17). It was not that his sight was dazzled and he could not see clearly. Nor did it happen that his gaze went beyond and failed to see the target. Rather, these observations were clear, plain, and in a solid, real form, in which there was no room for doubt or suspicion. And in these observations there was not only what has been described; rather, many other great signs of his Lord were also shown to him, and the reality of this universe was fully unveiled and shown to him directly.

Therefore, the matter of the Messenger ﷺ receiving revelation is an observation. In reality he has seen the higher realm. He speaks of it with firm conviction. His connection with the higher realm is direct. This knowledge and recognition is extremely solid and certain. He established these connections through his senses. This journey too was sensory and real, and these details being given are real, not allegories. The call of your companion is based on such certain observations. And when you deny, you are denying matters that he has seen with his own eyes, and you are doubting the descent of revelation. And you know well about your companion; you regard him as truthful and trustworthy. He is no stranger among you. Your Lord swears an oath to confirm and affirm it, and gives the details of what the manner of this revelation was, through whose hands this message is arriving, where the meeting of Jibril and Muhammad ﷺ took place, and what was at the Lote Tree (Sidrah)...

In short, this is a certain matter to which Muhammad ﷺ is calling. Now consider a little: what kind of people are your imaginations, fabrications, and so-called deities, and what is their fabled reality? What is the proof of the divinity of Lat, Manat and Uzza, whom you worship? You claim that Lat, Manat and Uzza are angels, but who has seen them? What is the proof that they are the daughters of Allah? What is the proof that their intercession will be accepted with Allah? Do you not have an argument or evidence? Lat was a white stone with carvings on it. At Ta'if there was a house and a shrine built over it, and attendants (pujaris) were appointed to it. Around this shrine was a large enclosure wall, and the people of Ta'if held it in great reverence, that is, they took pride in it. The Quraysh were the exception, since they had the Ka'bah, which was built by Ibrahim (peace be upon him). It is said that the word Lat is the feminine form of Allah, Who is exalted far above this.

Al-Uzza was a tree with a place of worship built over it, and it had curtains. It was at Nakhlah, which lay between Makkah and Ta'if. The Quraysh also venerated it, as Abu Sufyan said on the day of Uhud:

"Lana al-Uzza wa la Uzza lakum" ("We have al-Uzza, and you have no Uzza").

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Reply with this:

"Allahu mawlana wa la mawla lakum" ("Allah is our Master, and you have no master")."

It is also said that al-Uzza is the feminine form of 'Aziz.

The idol of Manat was at Mushallal, near Qudayd, which lies between Makkah and Madinah. The Khuza'ah, the Aws and the Khazraj venerated it, and they would put on the ihram (the sacred state for pilgrimage) for Makkah from Qudayd or Mushallal, out of reverence for Manat.

There were many other idols worshipped in Arabia, but these three were the great centres of worship.

It is said that these three names were the names of three angels, whom the Arabs called the daughters of Allah, and for this reason they worshipped them. As is the general course of things, these three gradually came to be worshipped in their own right. The common masses forgot Allah and began to worship these idols as absolute deities in their own right. Few people among them held the view that they were worshipped because they were the daughters of Allah.

Allah described these deities in an extremely astonishing manner, as is clearly evident from the text:

﴿Have you considered Lat, and al-Uzza, and the third one, Manat, the other?﴾ (35:02)

The wonder is clear from the words "Have you considered" (afara'aytum), which show that Allah regards their act as extremely ridiculous. After expressing this astonishment, He then criticises them, because they assign daughters to Allah and sons to themselves.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 53, verse 21:

"Is it for you the males and for Allah the females? That would indeed be an unjust division." (53:21-22 as quoted in the commentary: "Is it for you the sons and for Allah the daughters? That, then, is an unfair division.") This follows the strange mention of these idols. After it, the commentary points out that these three idols were in fact symbols of names of angels, whom they considered to be daughters of Allah. Their own condition was that they found the birth of daughters extremely repugnant in their homes, yet they felt no shame in attributing daughters to Allah. Yet they did not know much about the angels, nor did they have any information on which basis they might say such things.

Allah Himself criticizes them according to their own notions and their fabricated beliefs, and even ridicules them, saying how fine a thing they have said:

"Is it for you the sons and for Him the daughters? That would indeed be an unfair division. What have you kept for yourselves, and what have you kept for Allah?" (53:21-22)

The commentary on surah 53, verse 22:

"That, then, is an unjust division." (35:22 in the Urdu text's numbering; the verse quoted is ﴿تِلْكَ إِذًا قِسْمَةٌ ضِيزَىٰ﴾)

From a realistic point of view, there is no basis for this notion at all. Viewed from the standpoint of reason and wisdom, there is no rational or transmitted proof for it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 53, verse 23:

ان ھی الا اسمائ ........ ربھم الھدی (35 : 32)

"In reality these are nothing but mere names which you and your forefathers have devised. Allah has sent down no authority for them. The truth is that these people are merely following conjecture and the desires of their souls, even though guidance has already come to them from their Lord."

These names, calling Lat, Manat and Uzza and others "deities," calling them "angels," calling the angels "daughters of Allah," or calling the angels "females": all of these are mere words, but the meanings for which these people use them do not exist at all, and there is no proof for this kind of claim. Allah has not confirmed any such thing. Therefore there is no evidence for these claims. Truth has its own weight in its place. Truth has its own strength in its place. As for falsehood, it is weak and light, feeble and frail, and it has no power to grip.

In the second half of this verse, they are left drowning in their illusions and superstitions. The dialogue with them is ended, and they are turned away from, as though they were not even inside the discourse at all. Now they are made absent, and comment is made about them.

ان یتبعون ........ الانفس (35 : 32) "In reality these people are merely following conjecture and the desires of their souls." Therefore they have neither proof, nor knowledge, nor certainty. Their beliefs are based only on conjecture and guesswork. Their desires are their evidence, whereas in matters of belief and doctrine, conjecture and desire have no place. What is required in this matter is a truthful attitude that is free from certainty-less whim and desire and far from self-interest and aims, while they have nothing except conjecture, desire and worldly objectives.

ولقد ........ الھدی (35 : 32) "even though guidance has already come to them from their Lord." Therefore now they have not even these excuses left.

When matters reach the level of carnal desires, and decisions begin to be made according to desires, no human affair remains upright. Then guidance and preaching are of no benefit, because the reason for rejecting guidance is no longer that they did not know, but that they wanted it this way. First they have made decisions under the influence of the desires of the soul, and now they are searching for justifications. When the human soul falls to this level, then guidance is no longer beneficial to it, and evidence has no effect. For this reason Allah questions them with severe disapproval.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 53, verse 24:

Am lil-insani ma tamanna (35:42): "Is man to have whatever he wishes?" That is, that he may wish and it becomes reality, that his desires become facts. But the matter is not like this. Truth is truth, and reality is reality. No one, however much he wishes, can change facts and realities by his wish. Man is ruined by his wishes, and he falls into the pit of destruction only because of the desires of the self (nafs). Therefore, desires and wishes cannot change the true reality of things (haqiqat nafs al-amri). No one can bring about change or alteration in the realities of this world and the Hereafter. These are in the hand of Allah, who is the Truth.

The commentary of Sayyid Qutb, *Fi Zilal al-Quran* (Urdu translation), on Surah 53, verse 25:

﴿Dunya aur aakhirat ka malik to Allah hi hai﴾ (35:52). Here Allah mentions the Hereafter before the world (dunya), so that the word *al-ula* (the first/the former) creates a rhythm that matches the style of the surah and its rhyme. In meaning too, the Hereafter is the more important. It is the nature of the Qur'an that the adjustments made for verbal harmony (*muraa'at-e-lafzi*, observing the sound and balance of words) do not alter the meaning. The perfection and beauty of speech lies in its being suited to the situation (*muqtada al-hal*), both in words and in meaning, and being exactly fitting and appropriate.

Since authority over both the Hereafter and this world belongs to Allah, the idea of the polytheists that they worship the angels so that the angels bring them near to Allah is wholly false. The angels have no authority to intercede. On the Day of Resurrection, the right of intercession (*shafa'at*) will belong only to those to whom Allah grants permission.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 53, verse 26:

﴿وَكَم مِّن مَّلَكٍ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ لَا تُغْنِي شَفَاعَتُهُمْ شَيْئًا إِلَّا مِن بَعْدِ أَن يَأْذَنَ اللَّهُ لِمَن يَشَاءُ وَيَرْضَىٰ﴾ (35:62)

"Many an angel there is in the heavens whose intercession avails nothing unless Allah gives permission to whomever He wills and is pleased with." Therefore their claim is baseless. The preceding verse has also demonstrated its falsehood, and it has declared beliefs free from every kind of doubt and admixture. The correct belief is that the authority to decide, both in this world and in the Hereafter, rests with Allah, and the wishes and desires of man cannot alter the truth. Permission for intercession will not be granted without Allah's leave. Therefore, the final decision will rest in Allah's hand.

At the end of this paragraph, the illusions of the polytheists are refuted for the last time: the views of the polytheists about the angels are not founded on any basis.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 53, verses 27–28:

"But those who do not believe in the Hereafter name the angels with the names of female deities, although they have no knowledge of this matter. They follow nothing but conjecture, and conjecture is of no use at all in place of the truth." (53:27–28)

This final comment also shows that al-Lat, al-Manat and al-Uzza were connected with the fable that they had fabricated about the angels being daughters of God. It was a baseless fable, based only on conjecture, estimation and hearsay, because they had no means of knowledge by which they could comprehend the reality of the angels. To attribute the angels to Allah was pure falsehood. There was no proof for it except illusion, and truth is never established by illusions and fables. They had abandoned truth and certainty, so nothing else can take the place of that lost treasure.

When the beliefs of the people of polytheism had been brought to this point, showing how baseless their shirk is, and that those who commit shirk, do not believe in the Hereafter, attribute daughters to Allah, and call the angels daughters, their beliefs are founded on conjecture and illusion, then the Prophet ﷺ was told to disregard these people, and to leave their affair to Allah. Allah knows well those who do good and those who do evil. He will recompense both the guided and the misguided with reward and punishment. The authority over the heavens and the earth is in His hand; the affairs of this world and the Hereafter are His. He will judge everyone with justice, will not wrong anyone, and forgives minor lapses of those who do not persist in sins. He knows intentions and secrets, because He is the Creator of human beings, and He regards His creation as better than others.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 53, verse 29:

فاعرض ............ بمن التقی (23) ک (35 : 92 تا 23)

"So, O Prophet, turn away from the one who turns away from Our Reminder and desires nothing but the life of this world. That is the extent of their knowledge. Your Lord knows best who has strayed from His path and who is upon the right way. And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, so that He may repay those who do evil according to their deeds and reward with the best reward those who do good, those who avoid the major sins and the shameful deeds, except for minor faults. Indeed, your Lord's forgiveness is vast. He knows you well, since He brought you forth from the earth and when you were embryos in your mothers' wombs. So do not claim purity for yourselves; He knows best who is truly righteous."

The command to turn away and to disregard is given to those who turn away from the remembrance of Allah, who do not believe in the Hereafter, and who desire only the life of this world. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is told to leave aside those polytheists whose beliefs and conduct were described at the beginning of this Surah, and whose superstitious and fanciful beliefs were refuted.

After the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), this address applies to every Muslim caller (da'i) who has to deal with people of this kind: those who are heedless of the remembrance of Allah, who do not believe in Allah and the Hereafter, and whose outlook is purely secular. They do not look beyond this world. The reckoning of the Hereafter is not in their sight, and they see that the sole purpose of their existence is this worldly life. "Live merrily, for the world is a fleeting thing" (Babar ba-aish kosh ke alam dobara nisbat), and they organise their lives on this basis. Such people detach human consciousness from the notion that there is a God who governs the affairs of people, and that this God will call them to account for their deeds after the brief life of this world. In our own age, the followers of materialism and atheism are precisely such people.

Those who believe in the Hereafter cannot take an interest in people who are heedless of the Hereafter, nor can they live in step with those who deny it. The foundations of the lives of the two kinds of people are so opposed that they cannot walk together even a single step, since they cannot agree on any point concerning the conduct of life. Their values and standards of life are different; their goals are different; their concepts are different. Therefore they cannot cooperate with one another. They cannot have a common activity on this earth, because their standards, values and aims differ. The method of their striving will differ, and their purposes will be separate. When there is no uniformity or unity between the two, what interest could one have in the other? If a believer takes an interest in people who turn away from the remembrance of Allah and seek nothing but the life of this world, he is engaged in a utterly futile task, and he is spending his strength without purpose.

Furthermore, turning away and disregarding has another purpose: to ignore and not give importance to those who are determined not to believe in Allah is itself a goal. Those who are merely slaves of this world are disregarded because they are fit only to be disregarded. They are far from the truth; they are not qualified to perceive the truth. They stand behind veils, and there is a barrier between them and reality. They cannot step out of the circle and limits of this world.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 53, verse 30:

"That is the extent of their knowledge" (53:30). This level of understanding is very trivial, even though outwardly they may appear to possess a very great reach. They are short-handed, even though their hands may appear long. They are astray, even though they may be covering distances rapidly. This is because whoever is confined to this world in terms of his heart's perception and his intellect will go around in it like the ox of an oil press; he cannot move forward, even though this vast universe lies before their eyes. This universe did not create itself, and the notion that this world came into existence on its own is a theory that is self-evidently false. Nor was this world created in vain; rather, it has a Creator. And if it is supposed that this is the only world and this is the only life, then this creation would be proven to be in vain. Therefore, from whatever angle one considers this world, faith becomes necessary, and this part of faith also becomes necessary: that resurrection and reckoning in the Hereafter are inevitable, otherwise it would necessarily follow that this great and marvelous universe was created in vain.

For this reason, whoever turns away from the remembrance of Allah and remains occupied only with worldly affairs must be disregarded. This disregard is necessary so that one's concern, attention and effort are not spent on misplaced matters, and in order to lessen the importance of those whose interests are limited only to this world, it is necessary to turn away from them. Allah has commanded us: "Turn away from such people." Therefore, we should disregard such people, because obedience to the command is necessary. Let it not be that, like the Jews, we say: "We hear and we disobey." May Allah protect us from this attitude.

"Indeed, your Lord knows best who has strayed from His path and who is guided to the right path" (53:30). Allah knows very well that these people are astray. Therefore Allah did not consider it appropriate for the Prophet and his companions to busy themselves needlessly with misguided people, or to sit in their company, or to become their friends. Nor is it appropriate for them to know that this person is astray and that his activities are limited only to this world. He does not strive or intend to grasp the truth, and does not believe deliberately. He does not believe in the Hereafter, and all his interests are confined to the brief life of this world. Such a person should not be the object of effort.

The knowledge that is attained by these shortsighted and astray people appears outwardly very great in the eyes of the common people, and those whose hearts, faculties of perception and sense are ordinary find it effective in practical life. But this knowledge of theirs cannot remove from them the quality of misguidance, nor can it remove from them the quality of ignorance and shortsightedness. This is because the connection between this universe and its Creator, and the connection between human action and its reward and punishment, are both realities that are necessary for any true knowledge. Any knowledge devoid of these two realities will be superficial and will not be fully effective in human life, nor will it establish a sound moral connection between one human being and another. Otherwise all sciences will be regarded merely as technology, and will be counted as a decline of humanity. The more the technical side of knowledge advances, the more its human side declines.

The awareness that man has a Creator, that this Creator created him and created this universe as well, and that this human being and this universe share one mode of creation, transforms man's consciousness of life and of his environment. The worth of a human being's existence is established, the purpose of his existence becomes more comprehensive and exalted, and his existence rises above his limited family. His existence becomes greater and more exalted than his nation. His existence becomes more precious than his homeland. Man rises above class conflict and above all such formations and collectivities.

Then, the awareness that his Creator will call him to account in the Hereafter and will reward or punish him changes man's emotions, man's aims, man's standards and values. The very manner of man's thinking changes. The end of man becomes bound to his morals. Thus man's strength and his activity increase, because his ruin or his salvation depends upon a sense of accountability in his intention and action. Thus "humanity" becomes strong within the human personality, because this awareness awakens within man like a watchman. He feels that the final reckoning is yet to come. In short, believing in Allah and believing in the Hereafter is a very important and great matter, and it has a fundamental importance in human life. We hold that this matter is more important for man than bread, clothing and shelter. If this belief and consciousness exist, this creature is a "human being"; if they do not, it is merely an animal.

When standards change, aims change, goals change, and all concepts of life change, then there remains no common ground between one human being and another. Mutual interaction and cooperation no longer remain, rather not even mutual recognition remains, and people cannot even understand one another, much less be able to act justly toward each other.

For this reason, there can be no companionship, partnership, cooperation or dealing between a believer in Allah and a purely worldly, self-interested person. This is the truth and reality; whatever else anyone says will be mere show and a statement contrary to the command of Allah.

"So turn away from one who turns away from Our remembrance and desires nothing but the life of this world" (53:29). Thus, O Prophet, leave to his own state the one who turns away from Our remembrance and seeks nothing but the life of this world.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 53, verse 31:

﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, that He may recompense those who do evil according to what they have done and reward those who do good with the best reward﴾ (53:31). That Allah is the owner of all things in the heavens and the earth gives strength and effect to the belief in the Hereafter, for He who has decreed reckoning and accountability in the Hereafter is the owner of the earth and the heavens. Therefore He has the power to reward and punish. This is His alone to do, and He is also the owner of the causes of these things, and wisdom requires that He give complete and just recompense.

﴿That He may recompense those who do evil according to what they have done and reward those who do good with the best reward﴾ (53:31).

After this, those who did good deeds and who are to be given the best reward are specified.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 53, verse 32:

Those who avoid the major sins (kaba'ir) and the shameful deeds (fawahish), except for minor lapses (illa al-lamam) (53:32). "Major sins" means great acts of disobedience. "Fawahish" (shameful deeds) also means major sins, but especially those that involve indecency. Scholars differ in their views on "al-lamam" (minor lapses). Allama Ibn Kathir says that this exception is munqati' (disjunctive exception) (a disjunctive exception is one where the excepted thing is not a member of the group from which it is excluded), because lamam is said of minor sins, that is, small deeds. Imam Ahmad has narrated it: 'Abd al-Razzaq from Ma'mar from Ibn Tawus from his father from Hadrat Ibn 'Abbas (raḍiya Allahu 'anhu). He said: I have not seen anything more resembling lamam than what Hadrat Abu Hurayrah (raḍiya Allahu 'anhu) narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has written for the son of Adam his share of adultery, and he will surely encounter it. The adultery of the eye is the look, the adultery of the tongue is speech, and the soul desires and longs, and the private parts either confirm it or deny it" (Sahihayn).

Ibn Jarir has narrated, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la, from Ibn Thawr, from Ma'mar, from A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, that Ibn Mas'ud (raḍiya Allahu 'anhu) said: "The adultery of the eye is looking, the adultery of the lips is kissing, the adultery of the hand is grasping, the adultery of the foot is walking (to it), and the limbs either confirm it or deny it. If the private part then advances, he is an adulterer, and not one who committed lamam." Masruq and Sha'bi have also said the same.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Nafi' says (he is also called Ibn Lubabah al-Ta'ifi): I asked Abu Hurayrah about lamam, and he said: kissing, looking, signaling with the eye, touching; and when the private parts of the two parties meet and ghusl becomes obligatory, that is adultery. These are the views on lamam that are close to one another, but there are some other views as well.

'Ali ibn Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "Illa al-lamam" means except what has passed. This is also the view of Zayd ibn Aslam. Allama Ibn Jarir narrates from Ibn al-Muthanna, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Shu'bah, from Mansur, from Mujahid, who said regarding "illa al-lamam" that it means a person who commits sins and then gives them up.

Ibn Jarir has narrated from Sulayman ibn Jabbar, from Abu 'Asim, from Zakariyya, from Ibn Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Ata, from Hadrat Ibn 'Abbas.

"Those who avoid the major sins and the shameful deeds, except for minor lapses" (53:32). He said: This refers to the person who commits fornication (fahishah) and then repents. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"O Allah, if You forgive, You forgive all, and which of Your servants has not committed a fault?"

Imam Tirmidhi has narrated this in this way, from Ahmad ibn 'Uthman al-Basri, from Abu 'Asim al-Nabil. After that he said: This hadith is sahih, hasan and gharib, and it has reached us only through Zakariyya ibn Ishaq. Bazzar has also said that this hadith is connected only with this chain.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Buzay', from Yazid ibn Dhuray', from Yunus, from Hasan, from Abu Hurayrah (raḍiya Allahu 'anhu) (I think he conveyed this narration up to the Prophet) regarding this verse: "Those who avoid the major sins and shameful deeds, except for minor lapses." Here it is meant that he commits adultery and then repents and gives it up, or he commits theft and then gives it up, or he drinks wine and then abandons it. Then he said this is lamam and commission. A narration of this kind is also reported from Hasan, but it is a mawquf narration... In short, this is the second collection of narrations, and it indicates a completely different meaning of lamam.

In our view, this last opinion is more suitable for the verse that follows:

"Indeed your Lord has vast forgiveness" (53:32). With the mention of the vastness of Allah's forgiveness, it is most appropriate that lamam means the commission of major sins and shameful deeds, followed by repentance, and that the exception is muttasil (connected). The muhsinun (good-doers) are those who committed major sins or committed shameful deeds, and then quickly repented and turned back, and did not persist, as is mentioned elsewhere:

"And those who, when they commit an indecency or wrong themselves with some sin, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins, and they do not knowingly persist in what they did" (3:135).

The Quran calls these people the muttaqin (the God-conscious), and promises them forgiveness and a Paradise whose vastness exceeds the heavens and the earth. Therefore this meaning is closer to Allah's mercy and forgiveness, since Allah is Wide in forgiveness.

The conclusion is that Allah's just reward and punishment rests upon His vast knowledge.

"He knows you best since He produced you from the earth and when you were hidden embryos in your mothers' wombs" (53:32). He knows all your outward deeds. This knowledge is connected to every established reality that these people do not know, and it is Allah alone who knows about His creation. Allah knew even when they did not exist, and He was creating them from the earth. Then, when they were embryos in their mothers' wombs and had not yet opened their eyes in this world, Allah possessed true knowledge before their actual existence came into being.

With a Being whose knowledge is of this nature, if a human gives Him information about himself, this is extreme impertinence, because it is as though he shows Allah his reality, saying "I am this and I am that" before Allah.

"So do not claim purity for yourselves; He knows best who is truly God-conscious" (53:32).

Allah does not need you to inform Him about your souls, or to bargain over your deeds before Him. Allah's knowledge is complete, and His reward and punishment are just. Allah's judgment is the final judgment, and all affairs return to Him.

Now comes the final paragraph. This paragraph is very melodious and resembles the first paragraph. It explains the fundamental elements of the Islamic worldview, in the manner in which Ibrahim (ʿalayhi al-salam) established them for the Islamic worldview and the upright religion (din hanif). In it, humans are introduced to the Creator, and it is explained that Allah's will is active in your life, creating and highly effective. The signs of Allah's will are enumerated one by one, in a very effective manner that becomes attached to human intuition, and a person is so affected that he trembles. When this paragraph reaches its end, the reader's feelings are fully affected, a tremor overtakes the person, the hair stands on end, and he becomes overwhelmed and ready to answer with "Here I am" (labbayk).

Who is this person?

"Who turned away [from the path of Allah] and gave a little and then held back" (35:43) — and Allah regards his conduct as astonishing. Some narrations state that this was a specific individual who spent a little in the way of Allah and then stopped spending, lest he become poor. In his Al-Kashshaf, Allamah Zamakhshari identified him as Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him). However, Uthman's station and rank, and the spending he made in the cause of the Islamic movement without any delay or reckoning, are well known, and so is his belief. He knew well that every person is responsible for his own deeds, and that no other person can take on that responsibility. The narration that Allamah Zamakhshari mentions is contrary to this fundamental principle of Islam. The narration goes that Uthman used to spend in acts of goodness. Abdullah ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Sarh said: "Just as you are spending, nothing will remain with you." He was Uthman's foster brother. Uthman said that he had committed many sins and that he sought forgiveness by spending in the way of Allah. Abdullah then said: "Give me your she-camel along with its saddle, and I will take all your sins upon myself." So he gave him the she-camel, and they made witnesses to this transaction, and Uthman then stopped spending. Upon this, this verse was revealed. This narration is apparently false, because it is contrary to the Qur'anic principle.

It is also possible that this refers to a specific individual, and it is also possible that it refers to a representative type of people who are like this, for example, those people who spend in the path of the Islamic way of life and then stop. In the sight of Allah, such a person is worthy of wonder. By pointing to such a person, the noble Qur'an clarifies correct concepts.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 53, verse 35:

﴿Does he have knowledge of the unseen, so that he sees [the truth]?﴾ (53:35). Knowledge of the unseen belongs only to Allah, and no one other than Allah has knowledge of the unseen. Therefore, what is hidden for a person in the unseen world, he cannot be safe from. For this reason, a person should keep doing good deeds at all times, keep spending in the way of Allah, remain cautious throughout his whole life, and keep his deeds continuous. It should not be that he gives a little in charity and then stops. As for the unseen that is unknown, the guarantee that a person has in its defence is that he be cautious, keep his deed going, keep it continuous, hope for the forgiveness of Allah, and pray that his deeds be accepted.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 53, verses 36–37:

﴿Has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Moses, and of Abraham who fulfilled his obligation?﴾ This straight religion (al-din) is the one that has remained one and the same with all the Prophets, and its principles and foundations have remained one and the same. The books and callings of all the Messengers confirm one another, even though there are differences of time and place. These same principles were in the scriptures of Moses. They were the principles of the millat of Ibrahim (the religion of Abraham). Abraham was one who gave a very great proof of loyalty and fidelity. He fulfilled everything in full; he was absolutely faithful. Here, fulfilment (wafa') is mentioned in contrast to ikda, and ikda means cutting off (inqita'). In contrast to it, the word wafa' has come with a shaddah (waffa) so that there is no difference in the rhyme and melody. The question is: what was in the scriptures of Abraham?

The Qur'an verse 35:18 is quoted here as: "That no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another" (﴿وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ﴾). Therefore, no one can bear another's burden, nor can it be placed upon another.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 53, verse 39:

﴿And that man will have nothing but what he strives for﴾ (35:93)... That is, only what a person does is recorded in his account. Others' deeds are not written with his deeds, nor will his deeds be reduced to make up for another's shortcoming. This worldly life is a span of opportunity for action, so that a person may act and strive. When he dies, his opportunity for action ends, and the flow of his deeds ends with it. Only those deeds remain of which the Hadith gives explicit text.

"When a person dies, his deeds come to an end, except three: a continuing charity (sadaqah jariyah), or knowledge from which people benefit, or a righteous child who prays for him." (Muslim)

These three are in fact the ongoing deeds (a'mal jariyah) of that person. From this Hadith, Imam al-Shafi'i and his followers derive the ruling that the reward of reciting the Qur'an does not reach the dead, because that recitation is not part of their own effort and acquisition. For this reason, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave the Ummah no guidance on this matter, neither emphasized it nor indicated it, by explicit text or by allusion. Nor is it reported from any of the Companions that they dedicated the reward of reciting the Qur'an to the dead. If it were permissible, how could they have lagged behind in it? Moreover, matters of worship and the dedication of reward are those in which one should rely on the texts of the Qur'an and Sunnah. In such matters there is no room for opinion or analogy (qiyas). As for supplication (du'a) and charity (sadaqah), there is consensus (ijma') that their reward reaches the dead. (Ibn Kathir)

Wa-anna sa'yahu sawfa yura (and that his striving will soon be seen); thumma yujza'uhu al-jaza'a al-awfa (then he will be recompensed with the fullest recompense). ﴿And that his effort will soon be seen. Then he will be recompensed for it with the fullest recompense.﴾ (53:40–41)

Accordingly, no person's striving, deed or earning will be lost, and nothing will escape the knowledge of Allah or His scale. Every person will be given the full recompense for his struggle, with neither any diminution nor any injustice.

Thus the principle of individual responsibility is established, and along with it the assurance is given that complete justice will be done. In this way a human being's worth is determined: he is a rational, responsible, trustworthy creature, and he is free in his choices. He is an honoured creature. For him an opportunity for action is provided, and then he will be rewarded or punished for the deeds he performs in that opportunity, and in this reward and punishment there will be complete justice. Along with this, it will be absolute justice; no one's carnal desire will have any part in it, and no reality will be left uncounted due to ignorance.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 53, verse 42:

﴿And that the final return is to your Lord﴾ (35:24). So there is no other path. Every path ends at the court of Allah. There is no refuge other than Allah. Only His refuge exists, and one will be either in the Gardens or in the Fire.

The effect of this reality on human consciousness, human thought and human action is very profound. When a person realises that there is no option but to appear before Allah, he prepares his deeds and his self for that. In this matter he does everything within his capacity. His heart and his vision are linked to his ultimate end, and his gaze is fixed on the final outcome.

Having brought human thinking to this final end and final destination, it is then brought back to the affairs of the world, because in this world too all matters are settled according to the will of Allah, although man is free and responsible.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 53, verse 43:

﴿And that it is He who causes laughter and causes weeping﴾ (35:34)

This verse contains very great truths, and it has many shades of wisdom and many pictures. The first meaning is that Allah placed in man the capacity to laugh and to weep. These two qualities are among the secrets of human creation. Man does not know how he weeps and how he laughs. How these two opposite qualities and impressions have been placed together in man's intricate creation is not known. Man's psychological complexities are no less than his physiological complexities, and the physiological and psychological emotions and influences within him are interlinked, and his organs and psychological processes cooperate together in the process of weeping and laughing.

﴿He causes laughter and causes weeping﴾, that is, at the same time a person both weeps and laughs. Allah provided the causes, and He made these two qualities a complex secret: a person begins to weep on some causes and begins to laugh on others. Today one thing makes him weep, and tomorrow, because of the same thing, he laughs; today he laughs, and tomorrow, because of the same thing, he weeps. This is not because he suffers from madness, nor because he forgets; rather, these are psychological states. Psychological conditions change. Some values, some causes, some occasions and some motives are such that at times they make one weep and at times they make one laugh, and the human consciousness does not remain in one state.

It is also one form that one party weeps at an event while another laughs at the same event. The same event has different effects on different people. These are the conditions, influences, and psychological reactions to a single event. On one event, the same person sometimes weeps and sometimes laughs. Today he is pleased with some event and laughs, but tomorrow, when the bad consequences of that same event appear, he weeps. At that time his wish is: "Would that I had not done this." There are many people who laugh day and night in this world and will weep on the Day of Resurrection.

These are various scenes, various conditions and various seasons, and from this verse we can derive thousands of psychological states. This is about a consciousness. The more one undergoes psychological experiences, the more one will know that after every experience, the psychological situation that arises makes a person laugh or weep. This is the miracle of the Holy Qur'an: within a few words it presents a mirror in which whoever wishes, wherever he wishes, may see his own image.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 53, verse 44:

"...and that it is He who causes death and gives life" (35:44). In the same way, countless forms of death and life can be drawn from this verse, and a person can, by sharpening his perception, count them. One meaning of it is that Allah created death and life, as He says in another surah:

﴿He who created death and life﴾ (67:2)

The recurrence of both death and life continues in human society, so everyone knows death and life. But if a person wishes to discover the secret of death and life, they become a very deeply hidden mystery. What is the reality of death, and what is the secret of life? A human being cannot express their reality in his own words, nor can he determine any shape or form for them. How did life enter the frame of a living human being? What is it, where does it come from, and how did it enter every fibre of that human frame? How does it penetrate that living human or living universe? And what is death? How did this life leave and death arrive? It is a secret, hidden behind a veil, and it lies in the hand of Allah.

He gives life and causes death, and from this countless millions of forms of death and life come into view. In this earth there are many worlds of living things. In a single moment, many millions of things die and many millions come to life; life enters them, and until today only Allah knows this secret. There are deaths which become the cause and means of new lives. Since ancient times these forms have been appearing. When a person contemplates the centuries, even the time before the creation of man, many kinds of death and life have been operating here.

This is an endless number of pictures that appear. Through these brief words these pictures become manifest, and a person's hair stands on end. A person cannot keep control over himself or restrain himself, and it has a strange effect upon him.

"And that He created the pairs, the male and the female, from a drop of semen when it is emitted." This too is a great truth that occurs every moment in this world. Because this great event is constantly taking place, man forgets it, although it is a miracle and a marvel more wonderful than all imagined marvels.

A drop of semen, which falls, is a sticky substance of the human body, and it is in as great a quantity as sweat, tears and other fluids. After a time passes, it becomes something other than what it was, and then it takes on the form of man and woman; it becomes male and female. And how this miracle takes place! Had it not happened, we could not even have imagined it. This human being, who has a strong, vigorous and hard body: where was it? Where was it hidden in that fluid semen? Indeed, it was one of the many millions of parts of that semen. Where were its bones? Where was its flesh? Where were its skin and veins? Where were its hair and nails? And where were its qualities and capacities? Where was its character and its temperament? A cell visible only through a microscope, with many millions of other such cells present along with it, and all of them are in the one semen that comes out in the form of a drop. In that cell, in particular, where was the pattern of male and female? Eventually this pattern appeared within the embryo.

No intelligent person can reflect on this great truth and not be left astonished. It is simply impossible that someone should deny this great miracle and, out of arrogance and rebellion, say: "Brother, it simply happens this way, so go on, and that is that," and that the matter just happened by itself, "thus male and female came into being, and that is all; we know no more." Or that someone, trying to appear more educated, should say that these events occur this way because, by the nature of that material, this capacity existed, and that all living things have this power of reproduction. But that answer in turn requires further questions and explanation. The question arises: who bestowed this capacity? And who gave this instinct to everything, that it should work automatically for the preservation of the species and the continuity of life? Then, who gave these things the power to move from a weak state to a strong state? Who showed this path, who placed this desire, and who placed within each thing the properties of its kind, and within them the properties of reproducing things of that kind? Clearly there is a governing power which directs these affairs by its will, command and permission, and which guides every thing along a determined way and path.

And then, from this first creation, which is an undeniable truth, Allah turns man's attention to the second creation.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 53, verse 47:

﴿And that to your Lord is the final return.﴾ ... ﴿And that it is He who gives life to the next life.﴾ (53:47-48 as quoted at 35:74 in the commentary) "And that it is upon Him to bring about the second life." The second life is indeed an unseen matter, but the first life is evidence for the second. The argument runs thus: when a power first created man, it is able to create him a second time as well. He is the One who created the pair (male and female) from a drop of semen, which is your own observation, and He is capable of gathering these bones and this dust again and raising you up, because gathering bones and dust is not more difficult than producing, from a single cell within the seminal fluid, a complete being. This act can also occur a second time; for example, the process by which a drop of semen, from a very small germ, passes along a long path and takes the form of a complete man and woman. Through this same process, Allah will raise everyone on the Day of Resurrection, so that each may be recompensed with reward and punishment according to what they did. For the purpose of raising again is the completion of life, which was incomplete here. In the Hereafter everything will reach its perfection, so it is necessary that the technology of creation there be even more intricate than the creation of this world. Thus the indication of the first creation toward the second is of two kinds: first, that a second creation is possible; and second, that it is necessary that complete reward and punishment be received there, and that incomplete life be completed. And in this life and in the next, Allah makes whomever He wills rich and wealthy.

This passage is Sayyid Qutb's commentary on Surah An-Najm (53), verse 48.

﴿وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَغْنَى وَأَقْنَى﴾ (35:84) "And that He it is Who enriches and grants property." In the world He makes whomever He wills rich in various respects: rich in wealth, rich in health, rich in children, rich in contentment of heart, and rich in one's relationship with Allah. This last is the greatest richness. And whomever He wills, He will make rich in the Hereafter.

Likewise, He grants property to whomever He wills, whether here in this world or in the Hereafter. People are in fact poor and needy. This wealth and affluence can only come from the treasures of Allah. It is He who gives wealth, and it is He who gives property. This is something people actually witness, and among them are people to whom Allah has given, so they are awakened to the realization that they should turn their eyes towards the abundant treasury of Allah alone. The treasures other than Allah's are worthless and empty.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 53, verse 49:

وانہ ........ الشعری (35 : 94) "And He is the Lord of Sirius (al-Shi'ra)." Al-Shi'ra is the star which is twenty times greater than the sun, and it is situated at a distance of many millions of times the distance of the sun. Some people among the Arabs used to worship this star, and some regarded it as a star of great eminence. Therefore, the emphasis here that Allah is also the Lord of al-Shi'ra highlights its importance, especially in a surah in which an oath is sworn by a star, which mentions the journey to the higher realm, and whose subject is the belief in Tawhid and Shirk.

Here the long contemplative journey through the inner self (anfus) and the outer horizons (afaq) comes to an end, and after this we enter the valley of human history. The Qur'an gives great importance to human history and its lessons-giving traces.

**Wa annahu ............ tatamari (55) (35:05 to 55)** ("And that He it is who destroyed the first 'Ad, and Thamud, and spared none of them; and before them the people of Nuh, for they were indeed most unjust and rebellious; and the overturned cities He hurled down, then covered them with what covered them. So which of the favours of your Lord will you doubt?")

This is a brief survey, in which each nation is glanced at in turn. By showing its end, it calls human consciousness to awaken.

The Qur'an's readers already know 'Ad, Thamud and the people of Nuh, and these accounts are mentioned in many places. The word *al-Mu'tafikah* (the overturned cities) comes from *ifk*, meaning slander and misguidance. (The overturned cities were the cities of the people of Lut.) As for the statement that "what covered them covered them," the name of the punishment is not mentioned, in order to show it as more terrifying and greater. That is, whatever destruction you can imagine, whether ruin or volcanic upheaval, covered them, so there is no need to specify it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 53, verse 62 (part 1 of 2):

﴿فَاسْجُدُوا لِلَّهِ وَاعْبُدُوا﴾ (35 : 26) ع (السجدة) "Bow down before Allah and worship Him." In this manner the call is raised loudly, and after a long preface it is a cry that sets hearts trembling and makes even the hardest nerves quiver.

That is why the disbelievers prostrated when they heard it. They fell in prostration, although they were polytheists. They doubted the revelation and constantly argued about Allah and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

They prostrated in circumstances where they had already heard the dreadful outcome in the whole of this surah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was reciting with a deeply moving tone. Muslims and polytheists were all sitting in the Haram. He prostrated, and when the Muslims prostrated, the polytheists also fell down involuntarily. They could not withstand the powerful effect of the Word of Allah. Even Satan could not stop them. When the effect of this passed, they forgot both that impression and the fact that they had prostrated.

The reports that they prostrated on hearing this surah are mass-transmitted (tawatur). After this, people have interpreted and analysed the incident according to their own views, although it was not a strange event. It was simply an example of the influence of the Noble Qur'an, before which even the hardest heart is at first overcome.

This incident, whose reports have reached the level of tawatur, is the prostration of the polytheists of Makkah. I too thought it necessary to comment on it and to analyse it, but after that I had a conscious experience of this incident, and I reflected on it in my heart and understood what its real cause was.

Earlier I had read the reports known as the "Hadith of the Gharaniq" (the so-called "Satanic Verses" narration). This report has been transmitted by Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat, by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari in his History, and some exegetes have cited it in their tafsir of 22 : 25.

﴿وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا ... حَكِيمٌ﴾ (22 : 25) "We never sent any messenger or prophet before you, but when he desired, Satan interfered with his desire. Thus Allah abolishes what Satan throws in, and then Allah establishes His verses. Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise."

Concerning these reports, Allama Ibn Kathir said that none of them has been transmitted with a sound chain. Among them, the most detailed, the least defamatory of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the least tainted by superstition is the report of Ibn Abi Hatim. It is said: Musa ibn al-Amusa al-Kufi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Shaibi, from Muhammad ibn Khalij, from Musa ibn Uqbah, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Surah al-Najm was revealed. In those days the polytheists used to say: "If this man mentions our deities in good terms, we will accept him and his companions. But he does not speak of the other opponents of his religion, such as the Jews and Christians, in the same words in which he speaks of our deities. He only abuses and reviles us." This was a time when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions were being subjected to severe persecution, and he was very distressed by their misguidance. So he used to wish that these people would come to guidance. When Allah revealed Surah al-Najm and in it this verse came:

﴿أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ ... تَوَلَّى﴾ (35 : 33) "Have you considered al-Lat and al-Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other?"
﴿وَأَعْطَى ... أَكْدَى﴾ (35 : 43) "And gave little and was stingy?"

Then Satan, immediately after these verses, uttered from his own tongue these words:

﴿تِلْكَ الْغَرَانِيقُ الْعُلَى، وَإِنَّ شَفَاعَتَهُنَّ لَتُرْتَجَى﴾ "Those are the exalted cranes (deities), and indeed their intercession is hoped for."

Satan had added this rhyming phrase of his own. Every polytheist in Makkah heard these words, they settled in their hearts, and as a result their tongues fell silent. On hearing these words, they congratulated one another and began to say that Muhammad (ﷺ) had returned to his former religion. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) reached the end of the surah, he prostrated, and the Muslims and polytheists sitting in the assembly also prostrated. Walid ibn al-Mughirah was an elderly man. He picked up some earth from the ground and prostrated upon it. Both parties were astonished that everyone had prostrated with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Muslims were astonished that the polytheists had prostrated although they had not believed, prostrating without faith or acceptance. The Muslims had not heard the words that Satan had uttered, which the polytheists had heard. So the polytheists were satisfied that Satan had placed this statement in the Messenger's desire, and had placed in the ears of the polytheists the idea that these words had been recited by the Messenger. Therefore they prostrated in honour of their deities.

This matter became very widely known among people, and Satan spread it so that it reached Abyssinia, where some believers were living, namely Uthman ibn Maz'un and his companions. They were told that the people of Makkah had become Muslims, had prayed with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they also heard that Walid ibn al-Mughirah had taken earth in his hand and prostrated upon it. They were told that now the Muslims were safe in Makkah. Accordingly the Abyssinian emigrants hurried back. Meanwhile Allah had nullified the effect of this satanic act, had made His verses firm, had protected them from fabrication, and Allah said:

﴿وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ ...﴾ "We never sent before you any messenger or prophet..." When Allah issued His decision and abrogated the satanic rhyme, the polytheists also returned to their misguidance and enmity, and began once again to persecute the Muslims.

There are some reports in which the above passage (the Gharaniq) is attributed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), with the explanation that (God forbid) the Messenger wished that somehow the people would become Muslims and that some reconciliation could be reached with the Quraysh. As far as I am concerned, I rejected these reports as soon as I read them, because once they are accepted, belief in the infallibility of the prophets and in the preservation of revelation can no longer remain. These reports are extremely frivolous and open the way to the possibility of distortion in the Noble Qur'an. But the most important point is that the wording of the surah itself does not bear these words. Even those who have declared these words to be Satan's words cannot be correct, since it is not possible that they were uttered within the wording of this surah and that the polytheists took from them the impression mentioned in those reports. The polytheists were Arabs. They understood the Arabic language very well. When they heard the phrase "Gharaniq" and then immediately heard this verse:

﴿أَلَكُمُ الذَّكَرُ وَلَهُ الْأُنثَىٰ... مِن سُلْطَانٍ﴾ (35 : 32) "Are you to have the male and He the female? That, then, is an unjust division. They are but names which you and your fathers have invented; Allah has sent down no authority for them."

Did they not understand the meaning of this passage, and then listen to the following:

﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ ... الْحَقِّ شَيْئًا﴾ (35 : 82) "Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter name the angels with female names, though they have no knowledge of it. They follow only assumption, and assumption is of no use against the truth at all."

And before that they also heard:

﴿وَكَم مِّن ... وَيَرْضَىٰ﴾ (35 : 62) "How many angels are there in the heavens whose intercession will avail nothing except after Allah permits it for whom He wills and approves?"

These polytheists, who were Arabs and understood speech well, how could they prostrate together with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)? In that case this speech would not even remain consistent: the praise of their idols and the claim that their intercession would be accepted would no longer be acknowledged. They were not as dull as those people were who transmitted these reports, or composed them, and whom the Orientalists today embrace with both hands, or who, out of ignorance or for the sake of their own purposes, do so.

As for the prostration of the polytheists, it is correct, and it must have happened for some other reason. Likewise the emigrants may have returned from Abyssinia for some other reason. Here we cannot investigate the return of the emigrants, that they came back and then again went to Abyssinia. Yes, here the matter of the polytheists' prostration is necessary to discuss.

For a long time I kept reflecting on why the polytheists had prostrated involuntarily. One possibility that comes to my mind is that it happened in this way. The reports say that the emigrants to Abyssinia returned after two or three months. This too is an act requiring justification. In any case, while I was still pondering this point, I had to go through a conscious and practical experience, to which I have already alluded earlier.

Once, while walking at night with some friends, we heard the recitation of a reciter nearby. He was reciting Surah al-Najm. We fell silent and listened to the Noble Qur'an. The reciter's voice was very beautiful, and his recitation was also very good.

I kept walking along with that reciter. My imagination travelled with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) through the higher realm: then the meeting with Jibril (peace be upon him) in his true form, which must also have been a strange experience for the Messenger. Then we went towards Sidrat al-Muntaha and Jannat al-Ma'wa. I was going on with my thought and imagination while the reciter was reciting. This journey of mine continued as far as my imagination, my thought and my consciousness could accompany me.

After this, my feelings became focused on the notions that the polytheists held about the angels: their worship, their being children of God, their being feminine, then the scene of the creation of man from a drop of semen, the scenes of the embryo in the wombs of mothers, and the concept of Allah's comprehensive knowledge, as far as it was possible for me to grasp.

Then the final paragraph was recited, and impressions were coming upon me one after another: that unseen world which is beyond our sight is a vast universe; then the scenes of reckoning and accounting; then the scene that whatever path a person takes, its end will be a meeting with Allah. After this, in that world, everywhere some are weeping while others are laughing; billions of creatures come to life while billions pass away. And the drop of semen, the microscopic point, from where it begins, and how in the course of its journey it takes the form of male and female and becomes a powerful human being. Then my thought went to those towns that were destroyed, that were overturned, and upon which desolation falls, or whatever falls upon them.

Then the reciter recited the final cry:

﴿هَٰذَا نَذِيرٌ ... كَاشِفَةٌ﴾ (35 : 85) "This is a warning like the warnings of old. The impending event has drawn near. None besides Allah can avert it."

After this a last voice comes, and my whole body trembles in the face of that dreadful helplessness:

﴿أَفَمِنْ هَٰذَا ... سَامِدُونَ﴾ (35 : 16) "Is it at this discourse that you marvel? And you laugh and do not weep, while you are heedless? Do you dismiss it with mockery?"

And at last, when I heard the reciter recite:

﴿فَاسْجُدُوا لِلَّهِ وَاعْبُدُوا﴾ (35 : 26) (Recitation of the prostration verse) "Bow down before Allah and worship Him." My heart trembled. My nerves gave way, and my condition became such that I was physically exhausted, a shivering came over me, and it became difficult for me to stand. A flood of tears came, and despite my efforts I could not hold back the tears.

At that moment I became certain that the involuntary prostration of the polytheists of Makkah was something they were compelled to do. Its cause is the effect of the Noble Qur'an, which affects every person, and no one can remain unaffected by it. The verbal melody of this surah and its magical meaningful beauty create an earthquake within the body.

This was not the first time that I had heard or recited Surah al-Najm, but this time it had such an effect upon me, and such a reaction arose in me. This is the secret of the Noble Qur'an. In its reaction there are moments when a person hears a verse or a surah and immediately responds with "labbayk." These moments cannot be obtained by waiting. There are moments in which a person is joined to the real source of strength, and at that time he is affected, and he becomes something other than what he was.

I believe that on that day the hearers of the Qur'an were granted such moments. Then the reciter was the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). He recited with the deepest sincerity. His own self was personally present within the circumstances described in this surah. His person, his recitation and his sincerity were blended together in it. Under the influence of all these things, the hearers' nerves gave way, and they fell into prostration. When he recited:

﴿فَاسْجُدُوا لِلَّهِ وَاعْبُدُوا﴾ (35 : 26) (Recitation of the prostration verse) they all fell into prostration involuntarily. He himself fell down, the Muslims fell down, and the disbelievers fell down too.

It may be asked: you are describing your own experience and your own inner state, and you are a Muslim. You believe in this Qur'an and the Qur'an has a place and effect in your heart. These polytheists were not believers at all, and they denied the Qur'an, so how did they prostrate?

But there are two things which remove this doubt. First, the surah was being recited by the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) himself, who had received this Qur'an directly from its source. His whole life was composed of the Qur'an, and he had such attachment to the Qur'an that if he heard the sound of the Qur'an from any house, his steps would become heavy and he would begin to listen. Even in his own house, if he heard it, he would stand at the door, and would enter only when the recitation had finished. Moreover, in this surah there were mentioned those moments which he spent in the higher realm, which he spent with Ruh al-Amin (Jibril), and in which he saw Jibril in his true form. As for me, I was listening to a reciter. Therefore there is a very great difference between the two.

The second reason is that how could the hearts of these polytheists escape the great impact of the Quran, when they were hearing it directly from Hazrat Muhammad (ﷺ)? They knew that this is the Word of God, but they were indeed afflicted with mere obstinacy, and this stubbornness and obstinacy were also artificial. The two incidents that follow will show that they were greatly impressed by Hazrat Muhammad (ﷺ). They acknowledged his spiritual and moral powers, so their being impressed and falling into prostration is nothing unusual.

Ibn 'Asakir, in the biography of Utbah ibn Abi Lahab, has written, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Uthman ibn 'Urwah, from Ibn al-Zubayr, from his father, from Hanad ibn al-Aswad, who says: Abu Lahab and his son Utbah prepared to go to Syria. I also made preparations with them. His son Utbah said: "By God, I will go to Muhammad (ﷺ) and will cause him distress concerning his Lord." He came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Muhammad (ﷺ), I do not accept the one who drew near and hung down, until he was two bow-lengths away, or nearer." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, set upon him one of Your dogs." Utbah returned. His father asked: "Son, what did you say to him?" He recounted the incident, and he asked again: "What did he reply to you?" He told him that he had supplicated: "O Allah, set upon him one of Your dogs." Abu Lahab said: "Son, by God, I am not free of concern about his supplication against you." Nevertheless, we set out until we alighted at Abra', which is in Syria. We alighted at the church of a monk. He said: "O Arabs, why have you come by this route? Here lions roam about just as sheep and goats roam." Abu Lahab said to his companions: "Look, I am old, and I have a right over you, and this man has made a supplication against my son to his Lord. I fear him greatly, so gather your baggage in this church, put my son on top of the baggage, and then sleep around the baggage." We did so. At night a lion came. It smelled our faces, but found no prey. The lion leapt and climbed onto the baggage, smelled Utbah's face, and then mauled him thoroughly, mauled him thoroughly, and then crushed his head. Abu Lahab said: "Did I not say that he cannot escape Muhammad's supplication?"

This incident happened to Abu Lahab, who was among the most severe opponents of the Prophet (ﷺ), and was not only an opponent but the leader of the opponents. He would gather people against the Prophet (ﷺ). And in the Holy Quran, a curse against him has been recorded for all time.

﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he. His wealth and whatever he earned will not avail him. He will burn in a flaming fire, and his wife, the carrier of firewood, will have a rope of palm fiber around her neck.﴾ (111:1-5)

This was his true awareness concerning Muhammad (ﷺ), and how greatly he trembled from the supplication of Hazrat Muhammad (ﷺ), and he had no hope left for his son's survival.

The second incident concerns Utbah ibn Rabi'ah. The Quraysh sent him to Hazrat Muhammad (ﷺ) to speak with him, that he should desist from the movement that has caused division among the Quraysh and in which you criticize their gods. The Quraysh were ready, if you desire leadership, wealth, or women, to give them to you. When Utbah ibn Rabi'ah finished speaking, the Messenger (ﷺ) asked him whether his speech had ended, and he said: "Yes, it has ended." The Messenger (ﷺ) said: "Then listen to me." He said: "Very well, do so." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) recited the surah:

﴿Ha, Mim. A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, a Book whose verses have been detailed, an Arabic Quran for people who know, a bearer of good news and a warner, yet most of them turn away, and they do not listen.﴾ (41:1-4)

He continued reciting until he recited:

﴿If they turn away, then say: I warn you of a sudden punishment like the punishment that befell 'Ad and Thamud.﴾ (41:13)

At this point Utbah rose and placed his hand over the mouth of the Messenger (ﷺ). He became very frightened and requested the Prophet (ﷺ) to have mercy on his brothers. He returned to the Quraysh and related to them the whole incident, and said: "You know that Muhammad (ﷺ) does not tell lies. So I feared that punishment would come upon you."

This was the condition of the man who had not accepted Islam. His fear and impression are evident, despite the fact that these people were firmly set on denial with great stubbornness and obstinacy.

The same situation arose when these people heard Surah al-Najm from the blessed mouth of Hazrat Muhammad (ﷺ). They were so impressed and fell into such a state that they could not restrain themselves, and they prostrated along with the Messenger (ﷺ) and the Muslims, because there are moments when the Quran has a tremendous effect upon a person, and so they spontaneously prostrated. There was no "Gharaniq" matter in it, nor any other matter such as interference by Satan, and all the narrations on this subject are fabricated.
